spans.s:
Dhṛṣṭadyumna
(‘the proud and the radiant one’)
------------------------------------------
When Drupada, the king of Pāñcāla wanted a valiant son who could kill द्रोणाचार्य, his enemy, he performed a special sacrifice. धृष्टद्युम्न was then born, as an adult son, from the sacrificial fire. द्रौपदी too (wife of the Pāṇḍava heroes), was born out of the same fire, after him.
He was a great hero and a good ruler. It was he who conducted the svayaṁvara—the rite of a princess of marriageable age choosing her husband from among the assembled princes—of his sister द्रौपदी where अर्जुन succeeded in the contest and won her.
Since अर्जुन and the other Pāṇḍavas were disguised as ब्राह्मणस्, Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna secretly went to their dwelling place and discovered their true identity.
During the कुरुक्षेत्र war, he was made the commander-in-chief of the Pāṇḍava army. He successfully fought with many heroes of the enemy’s army, like Droṇa, Aśvatthāma and दुर्योधन. He beheaded Droṇa who had retired from the battle as per the sages’ advice. They had come to dissuade him from using the ब्रह्मास्त्र.
Dhṛṣṭadyumna was ultimately killed in sleep by Aśvatthāma.
